prompt: Give BookEntry a natural order by title and a separate BY_YEAR_THEN_TITLE comparator, then watch a TreeSet silently drop a duplicate title. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Comparable defines the one natural ordering a type carries with it, while a Comparator is an ordering supplied from outside, so a type can support many. Sorted collections judge duplicates by the ordering in use, not by equals: because compareTo here looks only at the title, a TreeSet on the natural order treats "Dune" and "dune" as the same element and keeps whichever arrived first. Handing the TreeSet the year-based comparator instead changes what counts as a duplicate, and nothing is dropped.
hints: String already knows how to do the case-insensitive comparison -- compareToIgnoreCase returns exactly the negative, zero or positive value compareTo needs.
Comparator.comparingInt with a method reference to the year getter gives the primary key; chain .thenComparing(...) onto it for the tie-break.
String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER is a ready-made Comparator<String> you can pass to thenComparing as the second argument.
